Its range covers hina dolls, kabuto helmet and armor displays for Boys' Day, hagoita and hamaya, including works by certified traditional craftspeople and named doll artists. sections.heading: The opportunity
paragraphs: Masumura Doll is looking for international partners who can present Japanese kabuto helmets, armor displays and traditional dolls to buyers who value heritage craftsmanship. The company was introduced to Partner Market Global through Japan Industrial Promotion Inc. (JIP Japan).

The partner profile is curated rather than mass-market: luxury retailers, art galleries, museums, premium hotels, interior designers and private collectors. Specific countries have not been named, so market priorities, assortment and the form of cooperation are open for discussion after a qualified inquiry.

sections.heading: About the company
paragraphs: According to its company profile, 株式会社 増村人形店 began in 1941 when Masao Masumura opened Masumura Masao Shoten in Osaka's Matsuyamachi, a district long associated with seasonal doll wholesale and retail. The business adopted its current name in 1981.

The current president, Kazuyuki Masumura, previously headed the Osaka branch of the Japan Doll Association and now serves as a director of that association and as a vice-chair of the Osaka retail doll cooperative. The head office is at Matsuyamachi-sumiyoshi 1-8, Chuo-ku, Osaka. The company states that it operates several shops in the district.
The president's message describes a philosophy of passing on the maker's intent honestly: craftspeople put care into each piece, and the retailer's task is to convey that to the customer accurately.

sections.heading: Products and craftsmanship
paragraphs: The core range is seasonal dolls: hina dolls for the March Girls' Day festival, kabuto helmet and armor displays for Boys' Day in May, and related items such as hagoita battledores and hamaya ceremonial arrows. The company states that it carries Kyoto-made hina dolls and Kyoto-made armor, as well as pieces by certified traditional craftspeople and named doll artists.
Which individual makers and ranges would be available for export, and in what quantities, has not been published and is to be confirmed with the company.

sections.heading: International expansion
paragraphs: The company's public website is written for Japanese domestic customers. The international programme described here comes from the client's brief to JIP Japan. No overseas shipping policy, export history or existing foreign partners are published, and none are claimed here.

Heritage armor and dolls can suit galleries, museum shops, hotel lobbies and interior projects as display objects with a clear cultural story. Whether Masumura Doll supplies finished pieces, curated sets or custom commissions to such buyers is a point to settle in discussion.

sections.heading: Who the ideal partner is
paragraphs: A suitable partner has an established client base in high-end retail, hospitality, design or collecting, and can explain Japanese festival and samurai heritage to its own customers. Experience handling fragile, high-value display objects, and care in presentation and after-sales support, will matter.
Partners should introduce their market, channel, typical client profile and any experience with Japanese craft in the first inquiry.

sections.heading: Considerations for importers
paragraphs: Helmets and armor displays combine metal, textile, lacquer and sometimes wood or natural materials, and dolls may include natural fibres and hair. Importers should check customs classification, materials and packaging rules in the destination country, and any cultural-property or antique rules that could apply. Contemporary reproductions differ from antiques; the company's pieces are described as newly made.

Shipping and insurance for fragile pieces, display and assembly guidance, and the seasonal demand pattern around March and May in Japan should all be reviewed with the company before a commercial plan is made.

sections.heading: Why this profile
paragraphs: The company has a long operating record under the same name and a verifiable head office in Osaka's doll district. JIP Japan has screened the company's identity and public information; commercial terms are not published and are discussed only with qualified partners.
